sections.title: Mission & Identity
data: Fort Campbell straddles the Kentucky-Tennessee border and is one of the Army's premier power-projection platforms, home to the 101st Airborne Division (Air Assault).
It also hosts significant special-operations forces, including the 5th Special Forces Group and the 160th Special Operations Aviation Regiment (SOAR).

sections.title: Tennessee or Kentucky? The Two-State Decision

data.subtitle: Neither state taxes active-duty pay, so the side of the line you choose matters for a spouse's paycheck, property, sales and car taxes, schools and home prices.
intro: Fort Campbell sits on the Kentucky-Tennessee state line. The post office address is in Kentucky, while the largest off-post community, Clarksville, is in Tennessee. That geography forces a decision other military families never have to make: which state to live in.

Kentucky does not tax active-duty military pay, even for Kentucky residents, and Tennessee has no tax on earned income, so the income tax question is only about a spouse's wages and other non-military income. Kentucky's 2026 rate is 3.5%, but a spouse who is in Kentucky only to be with the service member and keeps a legal residence in another state isn't taxed by Kentucky either. The bigger differences are property, sales and car taxes, schools and home prices.

rows: $74 wheel tax; one vehicle a year exempt for nonresident active duty
About $1.18 to $1.58 per $100 of value (2026); exempt if your LES shows another state, but not a civilian spouse's vehicles
3.5% unless the spouse is there only on the member's orders and keeps a legal residence elsewhere
CMCSS: 'Advancing' district; over 70% of schools A or B (2024-25)

About 6 min from Oak Grove; 26 from Hopkinsville

recommendations.advice: Look up the zoned schools for each address. In Clarksville, Sango Elementary and Rossview High earned an A in Tennessee's 2024-25 grades; Christian County's schools rated Yellow, the middle of Kentucky's five levels, in 2025-26.
Look hard at Hopkinsville: its typical home value ($193,328) is about $125,000 below Clarksville's ($317,914), though property tax is a higher share of value (about 0.92% inside the city).
Oak Grove: about 6 minutes from Blanchfield with no traffic.

Choose by the zoned school and your spouse's job. Renters skip property tax, so what remains is sales tax (9.5% in Montgomery County, 6% in Kentucky) and Kentucky's 3.5% tax on a spouse's wages unless the spouse keeps a legal residence elsewhere.

sections.title: Gates & Access
data: Open 24 hours: Gate 4 (TC Freeman Gate), Gate 7, Gate 10, Sabre I and Sabre II. Gate 1 is open 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily; Gates 3 and 6 and Mabry Gate weekdays 5 a.m. to 9 p.m.; Angels Gate weekdays 5 a.m. to 5 p.m.; Gates 2 and 5 are closed. Gate 7's commercial lane runs 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. (Fort Campbell gate hours, March 16, 2026).

Visitors without a DoD ID need a pass from the Visitor Control Center at Gate 7 (Building 7199, 7199 Glider Road; open 24 hours; 270-956-4488); Fort Campbell's visitor page (last updated October 2025) lists the Gate 4 visitor center as temporarily closed. Everyone needs a REAL ID or another approved federal ID, and drivers need their license, registration and proof of insurance. Passes can be requested up to 10 days ahead at pass.aie.army.mil and last up to 90 days.
IMPORTANT: gate hours change often. Always confirm which gates are open and their current hours on the official garrison page before you travel.

sections.title: On-Base Housing
data: On-post housing is Campbell Crossing, a Centinel Public Partnerships community developed with the Army and managed by WinnResidential Military Housing Services, with more than 4,450 homes.

Homes are available to military families, unaccompanied service members, reservists, DoD employees, retirees, and qualified civilians. Active-duty applicants need orders, an end-of-month LES, DA Form 31 and FC Form 1906; non-active-duty applicants pay a $75 application fee for each adult. Apply through the partner's online application.
Office: 2702 Michigan Avenue, (931) 431-2693, welcomehome@campbellcrossingllc.com; Monday to Thursday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Friday 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. We found no posted wait times, so ask when you apply.

sections.title: Schools
data: Families in on-post housing are eligible for DoDEA schools. The Department of Defense Education Activity operates 6 schools at Fort Campbell serving PK through grade 12.

Off post, the Tennessee side is served primarily by the Clarksville-Montgomery County School System (CMCSS); the Kentucky side primarily by Christian County Public Schools. Other nearby districts include Stewart and Cheatham (TN) and Todd and Trigg (KY).

data.Services: Primary care, pediatrics, behavioral health, pharmacy, lab, and radiology

intro: Whether to rent or buy is the biggest money decision of most PCS moves, and the answer is mostly about how long you'll be here and how steady the local market is.
rent: Your tour is short (about two years or less) or your orders feel uncertain.
You want time to learn the area before committing to a neighborhood.
You'd rather not gamble on resale timing when you PCS out.
Your BAH comfortably covers rent in the areas you'd consider.
buy: You expect to be here three or more years.
You want to use your VA loan and build equity instead of paying rent.
The market is steady and you could rent the home out later if needed.
You've found a neighborhood and commute you're confident about.
data.bottom_line: There is no universal right answer. Run your BAH against the rent and home prices above, weigh your tour length and the local market, and talk to a lender and an agent who work with military families before you commit.

intro: The first month at a new duty station is mostly logistics. Knocking these out early makes everything else easier.

steps.title: Line up temporary lodging
steps.text: Book on-base lodging or a short-term rental before you arrive. You can claim Temporary Lodging Expense (TLE) for a limited number of days while you house-hunt.

steps.title: In-process and update DEERS
steps.text: Report to your unit and finance, and make sure DEERS and ID cards are current for every family member so TRICARE and base access work.

steps.title: Start with the Housing Office
steps.text: Check on-base availability and get the housing office's read on off-base neighborhoods before you sign anything.

steps.title: Register your vehicle and sort access
steps.text: Handle base access and vehicle registration, and learn the visitor-pass process for guests. Bring your registration and insurance.

steps.title: Enroll the kids in school
steps.text: Contact the gaining school district or DoDEA early and bring records and immunizations. The School Liaison Office can help with the transfer.

steps.title: Set up healthcare
steps.text: Update your TRICARE region and enrollment so you can be seen at the local military treatment facility or network providers.

data.q: Should I live in Tennessee or Kentucky?
data.a: Neither state taxes active-duty pay, so it depends on your spouse's job, the schools and your budget. Tennessee has no tax on wages; Kentucky (Hopkinsville or Oak Grove) has lower home values, 6% sales tax and, from Oak Grove, the shortest drive. See the two-state section above.

data.q: Is there a DoDEA school on post?
data.a: Yes. Families in on-post housing are eligible for the DoDEA schools on Fort Campbell (PK through grade 12). Off post, the Tennessee side is mainly CMCSS and the Kentucky side mainly Christian County.
Campbell Crossing, a Centinel Public Partnerships community managed by WinnResidential, with more than 4,450 homes. Office: (931) 431-2693.
Fort Campbell is MHA KY106. Use the BAH calculator above for your grade and dependency status.

data.q: Does Kentucky tax my military pay?
data.a: No. Kentucky does not tax active-duty military pay, even for Kentucky residents, and Tennessee has no tax on wages. A spouse's Kentucky wages are taxed at 3.5% (2026) unless the spouse is in Kentucky only to be with the service member and keeps a legal residence in another state; local occupational license tax may apply where the spouse works.
